translationRepairs.before: Have you no desire for office?"
translationRepairs.after: Is there nothing you seek?"
translationRepairs.reason: 子無求乎 asks generally whether he seeks anything; it does not mention office.

translationRepairs.before: Will you not seek a post after all?"
translationRepairs.after: Is there nothing you seek after all?"
translationRepairs.reason: The added government post is unsupported by 子無求乎.

translationRepairs.before: Again the filial daughter Cao E, age just fourteen, her chaste and compliant virtue surpassed Yue, Liang, and Song; her father fell into the river and his body could not be recovered; E looked up to heaven and wailed, midstream sighed in grief, then threw herself into the water and died; father and son lost their corpses; afterward both came out; the people of the state pitied her filial righteousness and for her composed the piece "River Maid.
translationRepairs.after: Again the filial daughter Cao E, age just fourteen, her chaste and compliant virtue surpassed Yue, Liang, and Song; her father fell into the river and his body could not be recovered; E looked up to heaven and wailed, midstream sighed in grief, then threw herself into the water and died; father and daughter lost their corpses; afterward both came out; the people of the state pitied her filial righteousness and for her composed the piece "River Maid.
translationRepairs.reason: 曹娥 is the father's daughter, not his son.

translationRepairs.before: In Xianning 4 the court named him a doctorate; he pleaded illness and stayed away.
translationRepairs.after: In Xianning 4 the court named him an Erudite; he pleaded illness and stayed away.
translationRepairs.reason: 博士 is the court office Erudite, not an academic degree.

translationRepairs.before: Moreover for a plain-robed man to become governor there is precedent in Former Han; it is fitting to hear the brilliance to reward custom and air."
translationRepairs.after: Moreover, Former Han provides precedent for appointing a commoner as governor; his conspicuous advancement should be permitted to encourage prevailing values."
translationRepairs.reason: 宜聽光顯 means permitting conspicuous advancement, not 'hear the brilliance'; 風尚 means prevailing values.

translationRepairs.before: A tiger left a deer at his door; he told neighbors, they sold it and offered him coin.
translationRepairs.after: A wild beast left a deer at his door; he told neighbors, they sold it and offered him coin.
translationRepairs.reason: 猛獸 is an unspecified fierce or wild beast; the source does not identify a tiger.

translationRepairs.before: I mentioned it only because I do not need the silver.'
translationRepairs.after: I mentioned it only because I do not need the money.'
translationRepairs.reason: The passage says he had no need of the proceeds; it does not specify silver.

translationRepairs.before: Wen lifted three fingers—he died on the fifteenth day as he signaled.
translationRepairs.after: Wen raised his hand three times—he died on the fifteenth day as he signaled.
translationRepairs.reason: 三舉手 is three raisings of the hand, not three fingers.

translationRepairs.before: Gong Zhuang, styled Ziwei, was a man of Brazil.
translationRepairs.after: Gong Zhuang, styled Ziwei, was a man of Baxi.
translationRepairs.reason: 巴西 is the historical commandery Baxi, not Brazil; this complements the already-proposed idiomatic repair without duplicating it.

translationRepairs.before: His father was killed by Li Te; Zhuang for years did not remove mourning, his strength being weak and unable to avenge.
translationRepairs.after: His father and uncle were killed by Li Te; Zhuang for years did not remove mourning, his strength being weak and unable to avenge.
translationRepairs.reason: 父叔 names both his father and his uncle as victims.

translationRepairs.before: Li Te had his father killed; Zhuang wore mourning for years, too weak to strike back.
translationRepairs.after: Li Te had his father and uncle killed; Zhuang wore mourning for years, too weak to strike back.
translationRepairs.reason: The source expressly includes Gong Zhuang's uncle as well as his father.

translationRepairs.before: Bing Yu was Bing Yuan's heir: silent, careful, every gesture correct.
translationRepairs.after: Bing Yu was Bing Yuan's great-grandson: silent, careful, every gesture correct.
translationRepairs.reason: 曾孫 specifies a great-grandson, not merely an heir.

translationRepairs.before: Qiao Xiu, styled Yuanyan, was a man of Brazil.
translationRepairs.after: Qiao Xiu, styled Yuanyan, was a man of Baxi.
translationRepairs.reason: 巴西 is Baxi commandery; this complements the already-proposed idiomatic repair.

translationRepairs.before: When Li Xiong held Shu and annexed Brazil, Xiong's uncle Xiang and Xiang's son Shou both admired Xiu's name, fully preparing bundled silks and peace carriage to summon him; he answered neither.
translationRepairs.after: When Li Xiong held Shu and occupied Baxi, Xiong's uncle Xiang and Xiang's son Shou both admired Xiu's name, fully preparing bundled silks and a sedan carriage to summon him; he answered neither.
translationRepairs.reason: 巴西 is Baxi, not Brazil; 略有 here means occupying/possessing it, and 安車 is a seated or sedan carriage.

translationRepairs.before: When Fan Ben rose, a hundred clansmen sheltered under his staff.
translationRepairs.after: Soon Fan Ben and Xiao Jing rebelled in succession; Xiu fled to Dangqu, where hundreds of clansmen relied on him.
translationRepairs.reason: The current field omits Xiao Jing, Dangqu, and Qiao Xiu's flight, and reverses who relied on whom.

translationRepairs.before: Emperor Kang again with attendant censor regular summoned Tang; he firmly declined old age and illness and did not arrive.
translationRepairs.after: Emperor Kang again summoned Tang as Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance; he firmly declined on grounds of age and illness and did not arrive.
translationRepairs.reason: 散騎常侍 is Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance, not an attendant censor.

translationRepairs.before: Emperor Kang summoned him as attendant censor; again he pleaded age.
translationRepairs.after: Emperor Kang summoned him as Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance; again he pleaded age.
translationRepairs.reason: The office 散騎常侍 is mistranslated.

translationRepairs.before: Yu Liang recommended him with Zhai Tang; he ignored the doctorate call.
translationRepairs.after: Yu Liang recommended him with Zhai Tang; he ignored the summons as Erudite.
translationRepairs.reason: 博士 is the office Erudite rather than a doctorate.

translationRepairs.before: The man would not keep it; Fan said, 'If you refuse, neither of us owns it.'
translationRepairs.after: The man would not keep it; Fan said, 'If you had not retrieved it, how could I have gotten it?'
translationRepairs.reason: The source argues that Fan recovered the knife only because the passerby retrieved it; it does not say neither man owns it.

translationRepairs.before: Fan paid him tenfold the knife's worth and let him keep it.
translationRepairs.after: Fan respected his wishes and paid him tenfold the knife's worth.
translationRepairs.reason: 乃以十倍刀價與之 says Fan paid the man ten times the knife's value; it does not say he let the man keep the knife.

translationRepairs.before: When Ran Min seized the throne and offered the grand astrologer post, Xin wrote to Min, saying, "In old days Xu You declined Yao and with the realm yielded to him, preserving his lofty and clean integrity.
translationRepairs.after: When Ran Min seized the throne and offered the Grand Master of Ceremonies post, Xin wrote to Min, saying, "In old days Xu You declined Yao and with the realm yielded to him, preserving his lofty and clean integrity.
translationRepairs.reason: 太常 is Grand Master of Ceremonies, not grand astrologer.

translationRepairs.before: Chong heard and was greatly ashamed; thereupon he went to create his father.
translationRepairs.after: Chong heard and was greatly ashamed; thereupon he went to visit his father.
translationRepairs.reason: 造其父 means to go to or visit the father; 'create' is a lexical mistranslation.

translationRepairs.before: Liu Yao named him grand astrologer; he fled to Longshan.
translationRepairs.after: Liu Yao named him Grand Master of Ceremonies; he withdrew to Longshan.
translationRepairs.reason: 太常 is Grand Master of Ceremonies, and the passage says he firmly declined and then lived in seclusion, not that he fled.

translationRepairs.before: He answered no commandery summons; only with Yin Yong and Qi Liang was he friendly.
translationRepairs.after: He answered no provincial or commandery summons; only with Yin Yong and Qi Hao was he friendly.
translationRepairs.reason: 州郡 includes province and commandery, and 齊好 is Qi Hao; this complements the already-proposed idiomatic name repair.

translationRepairs.before: His sixth-generation ancestor Zheng, in the Shun'an era of Han, the ducal offices summoned him eight times, the state carriage five times—he took none.
translationRepairs.after: His sixth-generation ancestor Zheng, in the reigns of Emperors An and Shun of Han, was summoned eight times by the highest offices and five times by state carriage, but accepted none.
translationRepairs.reason: 漢安順之世 refers to the reigns of Han Emperors An and Shun, not a 'Shun'an era.'

translationRepairs.before: When rites were finished, he hid at Xie Valley of Linsong, chiseled a stone grotto and dwelt, ate cypress fruit to lighten the body, composed "Spring and Autumn Ink Discourse" and "Analects Mismatched Wefts"; disciples recorded numbered over a thousand.
translationRepairs.after: When rites were finished, he hid at Xie Valley of Linsong, chiseled a stone grotto and dwelt, ate cypress fruit to lighten the body, composed "Spring and Autumn Ink Discourse" and "Disordered Wefts of the Classic of Filial Piety"; registered disciples numbered over a thousand.
translationRepairs.reason: 孝經 is the Classic of Filial Piety, not the Analects; 著錄 describes registered disciples.

translationRepairs.before: Lu Zhong in Zhao, in righteousness did not seal his mouth—how much more when men will wear left lapel and not save them!"
translationRepairs.after: Lu Lian, when in Zhao, would not in righteousness keep silent—how much less can I fail to save men when they are about to wear their lapels on the left!"
translationRepairs.reason: 魯連 is Lu Lian, not Lu Zhong; this complements the existing idiomatic proposal.

translationRepairs.before: The character for roof is corpse above;
translationRepairs.after: In the character for 'roof' (屋), 'arrive' (至) stands beneath 'corpse' (尸);
translationRepairs.reason: 尸下至 explicitly describes 至 beneath 尸; the current field omits half of the character analysis.

translationRepairs.before: 'Roof' writes as corpse over a beam—
translationRepairs.after: 'Roof' writes as 'arrive' beneath 'corpse'—
translationRepairs.reason: The lower graph is 至 ('arrive'), not a beam.

translationRepairs.before: He studied under the technician Fan Xuan in Yuyang; Xuan marveled at him and gave him his elder brother's daughter as wife.
translationRepairs.after: He studied under the specialist Fan Xuan in Yuzhang; Xuan marveled at him and gave him his elder brother's daughter as wife.
translationRepairs.reason: 豫章 is Yuzhang, not Yuyang.

translationRepairs.before: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was repeatedly summoned as attendant censor regular and national university erudite; he pleaded father's illness and did not go.
translationRepairs.after: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was repeatedly summoned as Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance and Erudite of the Academy of the Sons of the State; he declined on account of his father's illness and did not go.
translationRepairs.reason: 散騎常侍 is Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance, not attendant censor regular.

translationRepairs.before: Later when Wang Xun became vice-director of the secretariat, he submitted a memorial again requesting summon as national university libationer, adding attendant censor regular; they summoned him; again he did not arrive.
translationRepairs.after: Later, when Wang Xun became Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, he submitted a memorial again requesting that Dai Kui be summoned as Libationer of the Academy of the Sons of the State, with the additional office of Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance; Dai was summoned but again did not arrive.
translationRepairs.reason: 散騎常侍 is Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance; the revision also makes the pronouns explicit without adding a new fact.

translationRepairs.before: His father Deng had served as minister of Changsha and attendant censor regular.
translationRepairs.after: His father Deng had served as Minister of Changsha and Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance.
translationRepairs.reason: 散騎常侍 is Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance.

translationRepairs.before: I wish to draw in fine words, with empty sincerity seek counsel; both may be appointed attendant censor regular, concurrently national university erudite; order the place below to prepare ritual and dispatch; do not follow routine, thereby delaying the hope of the vacated mat."
translationRepairs.after: I wish to draw upon their refined words and sincerely seek their counsel. Both may be appointed Gentlemen-in-Regular-Attendance while concurrently serving as Erudites of the Academy of the Sons of the State; order the local authorities to prepare the rites and send them on without following routine and thereby delaying my expectant hope."
translationRepairs.reason: 散騎常侍 and 國子博士 are offices; the current title 'attendant censor regular' is wrong and the current syntax obscures the appointment of both men.

translationRepairs.before: I wish to draw in fine words, with empty sincerity seek counsel; both may be appointed attendant censor regular, concurrently national university erudite; order the place below to prepare ritual and dispatch; do not follow routine, thereby delaying the hope of the vacated mat."
translationRepairs.after: I wish to draw upon their refined words and sincerely seek their counsel. Both may be appointed Gentlemen-in-Regular-Attendance while concurrently serving as Erudites of the Academy of the Sons of the State; order the local authorities to prepare the rites and send them on without following routine and thereby delaying my expectant hope."
translationRepairs.reason: Both current English fields repeat the same mistranslated office titles and malformed appointment sentence.

translationRepairs.before: He strung a soundless lute: 'Taste the music in the mind, not the ear.'
translationRepairs.after: He kept an unstrung zither: 'Taste the music in the mind, not the ear.'
translationRepairs.reason: 弦徽不具 says the instrument lacked strings and studs; 'strung' states the opposite.

translationRepairs.before: Sun Deng in his cave, Dong Jing in straw—
translationRepairs.after: Sun Deng in his cave, clothed only in woven grass—
translationRepairs.reason: This clause concerns Sun Deng alone; Dong Jing enters in the following unit.

translationRepairs.before: Dong Jing in rags—men like Liu Ling and Shang Ziping.
translationRepairs.after: Dong Jing lived among clustered shrines in clothes without a whole piece of silk and set forth a rule of integrity to Sun Chu; together these men hid their light beyond pursuit, successors to Liuxia Hui and Shang Ziping.
translationRepairs.reason: The existing proposal correctly rejects Liu Ling but still renders 柳禽 as a nonexistent 'Liu Qin' rather than Liuxia Hui (Zhan Qin), and it leaves most of the sentence untranslated.

extractionIssues.details: Continuous or clearly repeated individuals are split across records. Definite same-person groups include Xia Tong p014/p018/p250; Fan Can p041/p060; Fan Qiao p048/p050; Qiao Xiu p003/p125; Sun Deng p005/p247; Dong Jing p010/p248; Wu Zixu p036/p251; Jia Chong p028/p252; Song Xian p196/p253; Guo Yu p206/p212; Dai Kui p224/p233; and Tao Qian p242/p244. Recurring canonical people are also duplicated, including Confucius p001/p024/p066/p178/p210, Xunzi p002/p071, Yao p012/p033/p168, Shun p013/p034, Qu Yuan p015/p039, Liuxia Hui p009/p120, Sima Yan p046/p087, Zhang Hua p062/p081, Wang Dao p108/p137, Yu Liang p149/p159, Yu Yi p150/p160, Shi Le p164/p183, Shi Hu p165/p184, Fu Jian p190/p192/p213, and Zhuangzi p072/p180/p202.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Merge only source-supported same individuals, preserving all attestations, names, claims, relationships, and date evidence. Do not merge generic or merely similar names.

extractionIssues.details: Named or title-identified people in the source are absent as records or attestations: Liang Hong and Guan Ning (s0122); Li Quan 李銓 (s0158); Xu Meng 許猛 (s0223); the Prince of Yan 燕王 (s0224, retain source-form if unresolved); Han founder Liu Bang 漢祖 (s0270); Li Xiang 李驤 (s0428); Xiao Jing 蕭敬 (s0432); Zhai Fasi 翟法賜 (s0459); Master Chisong 赤松, paired with Wang Qiao in 松喬 (s0504); Gai Gong 蓋公 (s0535); Qian Lou 黔婁 (s0545); Wei Hua 韋華 (s0612); Zhang Xing 張興 and Duanmu Gan 幹木 (s0638); Meng Gongming 孟公明 (s0662/s0668/s0670); Xin Zhang 辛章 (s0673); Zhang Dayu 張大豫 (s0674); Suo Gu 索嘏 (s0678/s0681); Peng Hezheng 彭和正 and Zhang Tianci 張天錫 (s0701); Wang Ya 王雅 (s0757); Zhang Ye 張野, Yang Songling 羊松齡, and Pang Zun 寵遵 (s0834); Pang Tongzhi 龐通之 (s0839); and Liuxia Hui 柳禽/展禽 (s0860).
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Add conservative source-form records or attestations and link to an existing canonical person only when identity is definite. In particular, s0860 belongs with existing Liuxia Hui rather than a new Liu Qin/Liu Ling.

extractionIssues.details: The extraction omits explicitly present unnamed people needed for complete mention and relationship coverage: Zhang Hua's son sent to Lu Sheng; Dong Yang's wife; Gong Zhuang's father and uncle; Liu Linzhi's father; Fan Xuan's elder brother and that brother's daughter, who became Dai Kui's wife; Tao Qian's wife and children; and the student and two sons involved at Tao Qian's death.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Represent the source-form anonymous people and attach only the relationships directly stated in these units.

extractionIssues.details: p210 gives Confucius a surface and attestation at s0739, but the Chinese says 二本 ('the two roots/foundations') and does not mention Confucius.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Remove the s0739 Confucius surface and attestation while retaining his genuine mentions elsewhere.

extractionIssues.details: p248 assigns Dong Jing a surface and claim in s0859 solely because the defective idiomatic field inserts his name. The Chinese s0859 concerns Sun Deng; Dong Jing begins in s0860. Conversely, s0860 fails to attest Liuxia Hui because 柳禽 was mistranslated.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Remove Dong Jing from s0859, keep him at s0860, and add s0860 to the existing Liuxia Hui person after the translation repair.

extractionIssues.details: p060 is a separate Fan Can record whose supposed Chinese personal name is 武威, but Wuwei is the office/geographic title by which Fan Can was known in context, not another person.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Merge p060 into Fan Can and store Wuwei only as a source-appropriate office/title association.

extractionIssues.details: The extraction's all-durable-facts coverage claim is not met. Definite omissions include Zhu Chong's Erudite appointment; Fan Can's sequence of staff and court offices; Lu Sheng's editorial appointment; Guo Qi's and Wu Chao's appointments; Ren Xu's filial-and-incorrupt nomination, Gentleman of the Palace appointment, and commandery zhongzheng role; Sima Rui's later summons; Han Ji's Erudite appointment; Zhai Tang's and Zhai Zhuang's summonses; Xin Mi's Crown Prince Attendant and princely literary instructor appointments; Xia Tong's Grand Master of Ceremonies summons; Dai Kui's court and academy summonses; Gong Deng's Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance office; Gong Xuanzhi and Dai Kui's joint appointments; and Tao Qian's provincial, military-staff, and editorial appointments.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Add office/event claims from the cited units with exact source witnesses; distinguish offered, summoned, accepted, declined, and actually held offices.

extractionIssues.details: Existing claims lose source-critical participants or relationships: Gong Zhuang's uncle is omitted from Li Te's killings; Bing Yu is specifically Bing Yuan's great-grandson; Li Xiang is Li Xiong's uncle and Li Shou's father and joined the summons of Qiao Xiu; Xiao Jing joined Fan Ben's rebellion; and Fan Xuan gave his elder brother's daughter to Dai Kui as wife.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Repair these events and relationships after the corresponding translation fixes, retaining every named participant.

chronologyNotes.note: The extraction assigns Western intervals to all 253 person records, usually marked as external or inferred. Those years are not supplied by this chapter and this source review does not approve any of them. Preserve the native reign-era and relative-date witnesses and submit every Western interval to the independent date-audit workflow.
Precise native witnesses include Xianning 4 咸寧四年, Taikang 6 太康六年, Yuankang 8 元康八年, Xianhe 2 咸和二年, Taiyuan 20 太元二十年, and Yixi 2 義熙二年. Keep these source strings; no Western conversion is asserted here.

The fixed ancient years attached to legendary and early figures are external conventions, not chapter evidence. Several duplicates also disagree, notably Liuxia Hui p009 versus p120. Treat these as unresolved research claims rather than accepted chronology.

Several stored intervals do not match their own sourceDate labels: p040 extends Xianning to 290; p046 extends Taishi to 290; p235 begins 'early Yixi' in 395; p241 uses 334-340 for Xianhe; and p242 labels a 365-427 lifespan-like span as Yixi. These require fresh source review and must not be normalized by guesswork.

summary: Reviewed all 869 units and both English fields, plus all 9 existing proposed repairs. Found 38 additional or refined definite translation repairs across 33 units; together with the nonduplicated existing proposals, 37 units have a definite translation defect and 832 do not. The extraction also has definite duplicate records, missing named and unnamed people, two false mentions, a title misread as a person name, and substantial missing office and relationship claims. All Western chronology remains unapproved pending independent date audit.
